name: Lymphoproliferative Disease Associated with Primary Immune Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphoproliferative Disease Associated with Primary Immune Disease

criteria.description: Persistent or recurrent generalized lymphadenopathy lasting more than 3 months
Confirmed diagnosis of a primary immune deficiency by immunological and/or genetic testing
Histopathological or flow cytometric evidence of abnormal lymphocyte proliferation without evidence of malignancy
Presence of autoimmune cytopenias or other autoimmune phenomena
Exclusion of malignant lymphoma or other neoplastic causes by biopsy and imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: persistent generalized lymphadenopathy, confirmed primary immune deficiency, and evidence of abnormal lymphocyte proliferation without malignancy.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including immunology, hematology, and pathology.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically painless enlargement of multiple lymph node groups
Enlarged spleen due to lymphoid proliferation
Frequent bacterial, viral, or fungal infections
searchTerms: repeated infections due to weak immunity

common.notes: Destruction of red blood cells by autoantibodies
searchTerms: immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

common.symptomName: Chronic fatigue related to immune dysregulation
common.notes: Persistent tiredness not explained by other causes
searchTerms: chronic fatigue due to immune imbalance

common.notes: Enlarged liver due to lymphoid infiltration

occasional.notes: Inflammation and fibrosis of lung interstitium
Inflammation of small blood vessels in the skin
Peripheral nerve dysfunction causing sensory or motor symptoms
Reduced lymphocyte count in peripheral blood

rare.notes: Inflammation of CNS blood vessels causing neurological deficits

laboratory: Elevated serum immunoglobulins or hypogammaglobulinemia depending on immune defect
Autoimmune cytopenias (e.g., Coombs positive hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia)
Abnormal lymphocyte subsets on flow cytometry
imaging: Generalized lymphadenopathy on CT or MRI
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Interstitial lung changes on high-resolution chest CT
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with primary immunodeficiencies (e.g., CTLA4, LRBA, STAT3)
other: Histopathology showing polyclonal lymphoproliferation without malignant features
Exclusion of lymphoma by biopsy and immunophenotyping

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of malignant cells on biopsy
Chronic nonmalignant lymphadenopathy with autoimmune cytopenias

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes suggestive of malignant transformation
